transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Thu Feb 12 2026 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Eli (Redwood CSM), Olivia (CTO, Nighthawk), Marcus (Head MLOps), Sana (Procurement), Jonas (Infra)

Summary (auto): Customer leaning to extend; wants EU on‑prem pilot for residency, needs pricing and benchmarks.

[00:00] Samira: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, appreciate it. um we sent the renewal note last week, figured we'd walk through the capacity asks and the eu on‑prem pilot plan today
[00:12] Olivia: yeah hi thanks Samira, sorry running late, got pulled into another thread. we reviewed the usage dashboard — looks like our token consumption is spiking in morning windows, so we want to bump committed capacity.
[00:25] Marcus: to be concrete we're looking at roughly 2x of current committed GPU hours; the burst profile is also important, we need headroom for peak 30m windows.
[00:36] Diego: ok got it — when you say 2x is that steady state or committed only for peak windows?
[00:42] Marcus: committed steady state, with bursts up to 3x for short periods.
[00:47] Samira: that's helpful. pricing wise we can do tiered discounts on a 12‑month extension; i'll send an amendment with the 2x committed tier and separate burst pricing.
[00:56] Sana: procurement question — we need to know whether the eu on‑prem pilot will require a separate SOW or can it be an amendment to the existing contract. also SLA expectations, and does Redwood support our KMS/HSM?
[01:10] Eli: quick answer — we support customer KMS integration for Private via standard APIs, HSM options are available in the enterprise package. for SOW vs amendment i'll let Samira confirm but typically pilot scoping is an addendum, not a separate master.
[01:25] Jonas: technically we need assurance about audit logs and traceability — access logs for model inputs must be preserved but masked, and we need an export path for retention.
[01:36] Diego: yes on the runtime side our Private package logs token‑level traces and request metadata, and we can toggle PII redaction. the KV cache is handled in memory and we have an auto‑clear policy between sessions for the pilot, though we'll document the exact flow.
[01:54] Olivia: ok perfect. one thing — latency. our customer facing flows need <120ms median for short prompts; does dedicated plus on‑prem reach that? we've seen spikes to 200–300ms.
[02:06] Diego: latency depends on a few variables: model (quantized or full fp16), sequence length, and batching policy. for short prompts using a trimmed model with quantization we can hit sub‑120ms median on local on‑prem GPUs. some of the spikes likely come from cross‑region routing today.
[02:22] Marcus: are you recommending we move inference to EU on‑prem for all traffic or hybrid routing?
[02:28] Samira: we usually recommend hybrid: control plane in hosted, inference in Private region for residency and latency. fallback routing to hosted in other regions if capacity hit; that keeps reliability high.
[02:38] Olivia: what's the onboarding time for an on‑prem pilot? we have windows in March where infra is free.
[02:44] Diego: for a lightweight pilot we can do a minimal staging deployment in about 3 weeks if we get test images and network access; full production on‑prem could be 8–12 weeks depending on procurement and HSM setup.
[02:57] Sana: procurement needs a clear checklist — what network ports, what certs, and an estimation of egress costs if any.
[03:06] Eli: i'll compile a deployment checklist and share; it will include firewall rules, expected VM specs, and KMS endpoints.
[03:14] Samira: i'll also include a runbook for the benchmark — Diego can run a bench with their test set so we can measure token latency and throughput.
[03:21] Marcus: yes we'll share a synthetic prompt set and a sampling of longer prompts for tail latency.
[03:27] Diego: note we recommend including kv cache warmup in the benchmark to reflect realistic reuse; otherwise cold starts skew numbers.
[03:36] Olivia: good point. on pricing, can you give ballpark numbers now so the procurement team can tentatively budget?
[03:43] Samira: ballpark — doubling committed capacity would increase the monthly committed invoice by ~85% with tier discount; burst pricing applies above the commit. i'll put precise numbers in the amendment.
[03:56] Sana: and for the on‑prem pilot any setup fees?
[03:59] Samira: pilots usually have a modest one‑time onboarding fee to cover engineering support; i'll include that as a line item and an estimate for 20 hours of SE support.
[04:09] Jonas: on compliance — we need SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 docs and acceptance of pen test reports.
[04:15] Eli: we have SOC2 and ISO docs; i'll upload links and include redacted pen test summaries. we can also set up an architecture review with security engineers if you want deeper.
[04:27] Olivia: yes please, security wants a short AR call.
[04:30] Samira: ok we'll schedule a 45‑minute security review next week.
[04:33] Marcus: one more technical — kv cache eviction policy, how deterministic is it across restarts? we can't have stale context leaking across customers.
[04:42] Diego: eviction is per‑client namespace, and restarts flush the in‑memory KV cache unless you enable persistent cache which is only for internal workloads; for Private pilot we'll leave persistent off.
[04:55] Olivia: sounds good. anything else?
[04:58] Eli: quick recap and next steps — Samira to send amendment & pricing, Diego to share runbook and staging access checklist, Olivia/Marcus to send test set, Eli to upload security pack. we'll aim for benchmark week of Feb 24.
[05:12] Samira: perfect, thanks everyone.
[05:14] Sana: thanks all.
notes: There were a few transcription artifacts (company product names occasionally mistranscribed). Customer emphasized procurement timelines and security signoff as gating factors.
